title: Inventions and Discoveries
description: Big ideas that changed daily life.

entries.title: The Wheel
entries.summary: The wheel was one of the first really important inventions.
entries.body: Nobody knows exactly who invented the wheel, but it appeared about 5,500 years ago. The wheel made carts, carts made trade easier, and trade changed how people lived.
facts: The earliest wheels were probably made of wood.
The wheel is one of the oldest inventions we know.
Wheels made heavy things much easier to move.

entries.title: Paper
entries.summary: Paper lets us write and share ideas cheaply.
entries.body: Paper was invented in China about 2,000 years ago. Before paper, people wrote on bamboo strips or animal skin, which were heavy and expensive. Paper made books possible for many more people.
facts: Before paper, books were written on heavy materials.
Paper made knowledge much cheaper to spread.

entries.title: The Steam Engine
entries.summary: The steam engine changed travel and factories.
entries.body: A steam engine burns fuel to make steam, and the steam pushes a piston. James Watt made it much more efficient in the 1700s. Soon trains and steamships could drive anywhere.
facts: The steam engine was made much better by James Watt.
Steam engines powered the first trains and steamships.
Steam power made factories work without wind or water.

entries.title: The Electric Light Bulb
entries.summary: A practical light bulb changed the evening.
entries.body: Early electric lights were tried in the 1800s, but they burned out quickly. Thomas Edison made a bulb that lasted much longer, and in 1879 he demonstrated it. Soon homes and streets could be lit up.
facts: Edison's bulb lasted far longer than the first attempts.
Electric light changed how people worked in the evening.

entries.title: The Telephone
entries.summary: The telephone let people speak far apart.
entries.body: Alexander Graham Bell made the first working telephone in 1876. People could talk to each other over wires. Today phones send pictures, messages and video all around the world in a second.
facts: Bell made the first working telephone in 1876.
Modern phones use radio waves and satellites, not only wires.
The telephone changed how people kept in touch.

entries.title: Penicillin
entries.body: In 1928 Alexander Fleming noticed that a mould killed the bacteria in his dish. Scientists turned it into medicine, and during the Second World War it saved countless lives. Antibiotics are still one of the greatest medical discoveries.
facts: It was the first antibiotic medicine.
Antibiotics fight bacteria that make us ill.
